parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `stop`, `play`), the structural evidence confirms zero shared fields (`shared_field_count: 0`) and a null Jaccard similarity. More importantly, the two protocols encode fundamentally different domain contracts: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` is a low-level AVAudioEngine buffer-scheduling interface (exposing `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `makeRenderTapStream`, `volume`, `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerEvent>`), while `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a higher-level time-shifting playback contract (exposing `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `isAtLiveEdge`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`, `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerInternalEvent>`). Forcing a parent protocol would either over-constrain `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` with time-shift semantics it does not own, or produce a nearly-empty base protocol that adds no value. The overlapping method names (`play`, `stop`, `installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`) reflect shared audio-engine mechanics but diverge in signature (e.g., `play:() throws` vs `play:()`), making a common parent unsafe without signature reconciliation.
